system.summary: Letter signs with a few word signs, from the key register R9423, block 2_4 ('H. Wilh. [15]25'): A 9, B v, C Δ, D +, E 6 ... with und 9, auch Z, ch t; in this letter three of the register's name signs (⊡ ≈ ♀) behave as nulls or dividers, and five values are added from context (q a, Λ r, C s, H k, K z).

conditions.human_role: Project-level: DECODE login cookie supplied; problem posed with /goal; the user asked for a period German model. No target-specific intervention.

solution.what: Web search for KAA 4591 and Augurelio ciphers
DECODE record list from the API dump (141 records in the volume); images of the 14 targets and 30 neighbouring keys fetched with the cookie
R9423 key-register block 2_4 (Hz. Wilhelm) applied to R9367
Annealing with nulls allowed on R9367 (de-1500s, homophone caps): failed
R9423 block 2_4 read at zoom (keys9423/2_4_zoom.txt) and the frequent signs re-matched by shape: the key fits; ⊡ ≈ ♀ are nulls/dividers; five values added from context; reading in r9367/reading.txt

Split under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026) from kaa4591 (catalogue 161), whose fourteen records are letters in at least six systems: System A′ stays in kaa4591; Łaski's System B is kaa4591b; R9325 is fulda1576; R9367, R9416, R9424 and R9319 are r9367, r9416, r9424 and r9319; R9291 is a key fragment. Words of the decoded runs counted with measure.py.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): r9367/transcription.txt + signs.txt, the rough reading r9367/reading.txt (unread signs marked); key copied from NOTES.md and the reading header to texts/key.md, with r9367/key_match.md

Reading audit (George Lasry's test: can a reader build coherent sentences and translate them?). r9367/reading.txt read line by line: the cipher runs carry unread signs mid-word in most lines ('{s w a r d e [#] i n l?}', '{sa ber vir bar niwt [#] ...}'); only a few phrases assemble (docs/_check_reading.py: 14 of 35 sentences clean, mostly the clear German). Relabelled decoded, not read; class read in part -> not read, method read with known key -> not solved (key kept as a part); fraction_read 0.545 -> 0.

outcome.method_basis: Block 2_4 of the key register R9423 in the same volume, matched by shape and extended by five values (read with known key, recorded under parts), decodes the cipher runs only into phrases with unread signs mid-word; no cipher sentence can be built.
outcome.fraction_read_source: 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: the one document's cipher does not build sentences, so nothing counts as read (0). Withdrawn as a reading figure: 0.545, measure.py over the {..} runs of r9367/reading.txt (78 of 143 words), an upper bound that counted words, not sentences.
outcome.notes: Son to father, Monday after Palm Sunday 1535: questioned about strange matters and denied everything; taken for a poor writer; fears for his person; the Turks are coming up; a name like Nothaft; postscript on a Friedrich and Schmalkalden(?).

texts.label: KAA 4591 f. 169, 22 March 1535
texts.summary: A son to his father, Monday after Palm Sunday 1535, in German with cipher passages: he was questioned about strange matters and denied everything, is taken for a poor writer and sent to learn, fears for his person, and reports the Turks coming up; a postscript names a Friedrich and 'Schmalcz' (Schmalkalden?). The cipher runs are read in part with key block 2_4 of the register R9423 (# and O open).
texts.note: Per-line working reading: clear German in bars, decoded cipher in braces with '_', '[#]' and '?' marks; most cipher runs have unread signs mid-word ('{s w a r d e [#] i n l?}'), so the cipher sentences cannot be assembled beyond a few phrases (reading audit, 22 Oct 2026).

parts.label: R9367 cipher runs (register key 2_4 applied; decoded, not read)
parts.basis: R9423 block 2_4, re-matched by shape, plus five values from the letter; phrases only (seltsam khinst gefragt, aber alles verlaugnet, Tirckhen herauf ziechen). Decoded, not read (reading audit, 22 Oct 2026).
